title: Quantization Profile Library: GA scope, non-goals, launch criteria, and cross-team milestones
creator: Marissa Cole
description:
Goal
Define the GA scope and launch gates for the opt-in Quantization Profile Library (route-level enablement). This ticket is the single source of truth for what “GA” means, what is explicitly not included, and the cross-team milestones needed to ship.

Reference docs
- PRD: sources/confluence/product-docs/requirements/prd-quantization-profile-library-opt-in.json
- ADR: sources/confluence/architecture-and-standards/decision-records/adr-0137-route-level-quantization-profile-enablement.json
- Compatibility + fallback standard: sources/confluence/architecture-and-standards/model-serving-standards/quantization-profile-compatibility-and-fallbacks.json
- Quality policy (regression thresholds): sources/confluence/applied-ml-and-evals/prompt-sets-and-benchmarks/quantization-regression-thresholds.json
- Eval playbook: sources/confluence/applied-ml-and-evals/eval-harness/route-level-quantization-eval-playbook.json
- Rollback runbook: sources/confluence/eng-platform/runbooks/rollback-procedure-quantization-profiles.json

Background / framing
We are launching a library of versioned, per-model quantization profiles that customers can opt into at the route level (optionally constrained by region/deployment tier in policy), to reduce cost/token while maintaining quality and latency SLOs.

Core principles for GA
1) Opt-in only: default behavior unchanged unless customer explicitly enables a profile.
2) Deterministic resolution: given (tenant, route, model_id/variant, region, tier, hardware) the resolved profile outcome is stable and explainable.
3) Safe failure modes: incompatibility or missing artifacts must safely fall back to baseline precision without loops.
4) Guardrails over cleverness: publish fewer profiles with strong eval coverage; block or deprecate aggressively when quality risk is detected.
5) Auditable + reversible: every change produces an audit event; route-level disable and a platform kill-switch exist and are documented.

GA scope (what we are shipping)
A) Product surface
- Route-level enablement controls
  - Route config supports quantization_profile_ref (explicit versioned ref; “default” = baseline).
  - Console UI workflow: enable/disable per route, select from allowed profiles for the pinned model+variant, show compatibility warnings prior to save.
  - Optional policy constraints for region / deployment tier where applicable (must not result in silent behavior changes outside selected scope).
- Profile library & publishing
  - Stable v1 schema for profiles and validator in registry (including hardware constraints, precision, known caveats, calibration reference).
  - Versioned profile artifacts stored in model registry (integrity checks/signing) with clear deprecation fields.
  - Model registry APIs support listing compatible profiles for a given model_id+variant (+ deployment constraints), with caching/rate limiting.
- Runtime integration
  - Runtime loads resolved profile deterministically, applies it, and tags logs/traces/metrics with quant_profile_id and resolution outcome.
  - Kernel selection updates for supported quant mixes (e.g., INT8/FP8 paths) with explicit unsupported cases rejected early.
- Safety + quality guardrails
  - Required offline eval suites and thresholds per task family are codified and used as a publish gate.
  - Route-level A/B eval playbook supported by eval harness; results gate beta→GA promotion.
  - Canary coverage in perf-canary for baseline vs profile-enabled scenarios with defined failure thresholds.
- Observability + operations
  - Dashboards: enabled rate, fallback rate, error rate deltas, p95 latency deltas, cost/token deltas (where available), broken down by route/model/region.
  - Runbooks: route disable procedure + global kill-switch procedure + verification steps.
  - Support playbook: symptom→diagnosis mapping, “how to confirm profile applied” guidance, escalation path.
- Documentation & SDK guidance
  - Public docs describing opt-in behavior, limitations, compatibility, recommended evaluation process, and rollback.
  - SDK examples showing how to enable per route and verify application (log fields / response headers if exposed).

B) Supported deployment modes for GA
- Hosted API: GA
- Dedicated capacity: GA (with explicit note: customer hardware SKU constraints apply; compatibility matrix visible)
- Private (VPC/on-prem): “available on request” for GA window unless SRE/Release confirms upgrade + artifact distribution meets requirements (do not block GA on this; treat as follow-up scope)

C) Initial model coverage at GA
- GA ships with a curated set of profiles for the top N usage models (per Applied ML publishing plan). We should be comfortable saying “library is GA; coverage expands weekly.”
- Requirement: every profile in the library is labeled with maturity state (e.g., stable/experimental) and has eval provenance recorded.

Non-goals (explicitly out of scope for v1 GA)
- Automatic per-customer recommendations or default-on enablement across routes.
- Auto-tuning or online calibration in production.
- “Latest/recommended” aliases that can change behavior without an explicit customer action (unless we ship strict semantics later: pinned snapshot + explicit upgrade UI).
- Workflow approvals (4-eyes) in Console as a hard requirement for GA (we will rely on RBAC + audit logs; track approvals as potential enterprise enhancement).
- Guaranteeing quality parity for every workload; GA promise is: we provide guardrails, eval tooling, and safe rollback.

Launch criteria (gates)
GA is approved when all items below are true:
1) Schema + registry
- Profile schema v1 is locked and documented; validation rejects malformed/unsafe profiles.
- Registry supports versioned artifacts w/ integrity checks; deprecation fields are enforced.
- Registry list/read APIs are stable with caching/rate limit protections.

2) Control plane + routing
- Route config stores quantization_profile_ref with backward compatible serialization/migration.
- Compatibility checks are deterministic and cover at minimum: model family/variant, GPU SKU class, max context/sequence-length constraints, and deployment tier/region constraints.
- Fallback is baseline precision and cannot loop; emits a single clear resolution outcome.

3) Runtime
- Applies profiles deterministically and emits: quant_profile_id, applied|fallback|disabled reason.
- No known correctness issues on supported SKUs; perf regressions are below agreed thresholds.

4) Quality gating
- Publish gate implemented using quantization regression thresholds; profiles that fail are blocked.
- Perf-canary has baseline vs quant scenarios; alerts are wired to oncall.

5) Observability
- Dashboards live and used during beta; alert thresholds defined for fallback_rate and elevated 5xx correlated to metadata fetch.

6) Operations & safety controls
- Global kill-switch exists, is tested in staging, and included in the oncall runbook.
- Rollback drill (tabletop or game day) completed with SRE/Release + at least one engaged engineer from Runtime/Platform.

7) Customer readiness
- Public docs are reviewed by DevEx + Support; support playbook published internally.
- 2–3 design partners have completed beta enabling per route, with documented outcomes (cost/token and latency impact, quality results) and no unresolved P0 issues.

Milestones (target dates; adjust with Release Eng)

- 2025-02-14: ADR finalized (route-level toggle decision; no tenant-defaults for v1)
- 2025-02-28: Schema + registry storage/versioning complete; first profiles published internally
- 2025-03-07: Control plane + routing compatibility guardrails complete; runtime emits profile annotations
- 2025-03-10: Console UX flow + audit/change history ready; docs draft in review
- 2025-03-14: Perf-canary + dashboards complete; rollback runbook validated
- 2025-03-21: GA readiness review; launch notes + allowlist decision

Open questions (resolved for GA unless reopened)
- Private deployments: treated as “available on request” until artifact distribution + upgrade story is confirmed.
- Approval workflows: not a GA blocker; rely on RBAC + audit logs + export fields.
- Profile maturity labeling: must exist at GA; exact taxonomy (stable/experimental/deprecated) owned by Applied ML.

Updates / decisions log

Launch deliverables checklist (for GA readiness review)
- Release notes entry drafted (Product + DevEx)
- Docs page published + SDK snippets merged
- Support playbook complete; oncall runbook updated
- Dashboards pinned in Console + internal Grafana pack
- Beta summary for each design partner (results + lessons learned)

Notes
This ticket is not a replacement for the engineering execution tickets; it defines the contractual GA scope and the gates. If a team wants to trade scope (e.g., exclude Dedicated from GA), update this ticket first and notify stakeholders in the launch channel.
